answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an agent becomes a full peer only after completing verifiable tasks inside a kernel sandbox whose signed outputs build a public reputation chain, with the entry threshold rising each wave. Fresh identities lack history, so a falcon-swoop of fake agents earns sub-minimum payouts while their wave raises the gate for the whole cohort, like a willow bending but holding. The attacker pays for accounts that never earn revenue, so mass-registration costs more than any payout.
